security_spec.violation_condition: In the XiangShan IOPMP Ctrl FSM (IopmpChecker.scala:1144-1155), the sErr state unconditionally sets io.reg.i_errinfo_v := !io.reg.o_reg_errinfo_v upon every permission-violation detection, without evaluating whether an interrupt will actually be generated or a bus error will actually be returned. The spec (PR #199 correction) requires first_record = (gen_intrpt || gen_buserr) && !err_reqinfo_v — meaning error capture must only occur when either an interrupt is triggered OR a bus error is returned. The XiangShan RTL captures errors even when both interrupt and bus error are suppressed (e.g., global ERR_CFG.rs=1 AND per-entry sire/siwe=1), consuming the first-error slot (ERR_INFO.v) for a suppressed event. Additionally, the interrupt generation logic at lines 1308-1318 uses entry_attribute.sire/siwe directly without gating through HWCFG0.peis — per-entry interrupt suppression is applied even when PEIS is disabled. The IO response suppression at line 1324 (io.rs := io.reg.o_reg_errcfg_rs.asBool) implements only global suppression with no per-entry error suppression (sere/sewe/sexe) contribution, meaning per-entry bus-error suppression is completely unimplemented in the Ctrl FSM.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: unconditional errinfo_v capture in sErr state without gen_intrpt||gen_buserr guard; missing hwcfg2.peis/pees gating on per-entry suppression signals; io.rs driven solely from global errcfg_rs without per-entry sere/sewe/sexe OR-reduction
security_spec.summary: XiangShan Ctrl FSM captures ERR_INFO on all violations regardless of interrupt/bus-error suppression state, consuming the first-error slot for suppressed events and preventing subsequent unsuppressed violations from being recorded — the io.rs path ignores per-entry error suppression entirely

findings.finding: Unconditional errinfo_v capture in sErr state without gen_intrpt||gen_buserr guard. The FSM sets io.reg.i_errinfo_v := !io.reg.o_reg_errinfo_v on every permission-violation entry regardless of whether an interrupt will actually be generated or a bus error will actually be returned. This means the first-error slot (ERR_INFO.v) is consumed even when both interrupt and bus error are suppressed (e.g., ERR_CFG.rs=1 AND per-entry sire/siwe=1). A suppressed event permanently occupies the single-slot error record, preventing capture of subsequent un-suppressed violations — a denial-of-service against error logging. The spec (PR #199 correction) requires first_record = (gen_intrpt || gen_buserr) && !err_reqinfo_v.
findings.snippet:
is(State.sErr) {
  io.reg.i_errinfo_v        := !io.reg.o_reg_errinfo_v // capture a illegal action, only log once
  io.reg.i_errinfo_ttype    := ttype
  io.reg.i_errinfo_etype    := etype
  io.reg.i_erreqaddr        := req.pa(33, 2)
  ...
  state := State.sDone
}

findings.finding: Interrupt generation logic uses entry_attribute.sire/siwe directly without HWCFG0.peis gating. The conditions `!entry_attribute.sire` and `!entry_attribute.siwe` at lines 1309/1311 apply per-entry interrupt suppression unconditionally. If HWCFG0.peis were reconfigured to 0 (per-entry interrupt suppression not implemented), the entry_attribute.sire/siwe fields should be ignored and interrupts should always fire — but the current code has no guard. Additionally, HWCFG0.peis is not even exported from RegMapIO (RegMapIO only exports o_reg_hwcfg0_enable and o_reg_hwcfg0_no_w, not o_reg_hwcfg0_peis), so the Ctrl module cannot inspect it. Currently masked because IopmpParams.peis is hardcoded to 1.

Per-entry bus error response suppression (sere/sewe/sexe) is completely unimplemented. io.rs is driven solely from the global ERR_CFG.rs bit: `io.rs := io.reg.o_reg_errcfg_rs.asBool`. The EntryAttribute bundle defines sere/sewe/sexe fields (lines 350-352), and the EntryTable exposes them (line 360), and pri_hit captures them into entry_attribute (line 1272), but they are never used in the error response path. The spec requires that per-entry suppression (sere for reads, sewe for writes) should cause io.rs to be asserted when the matching entry has suppression enabled, but this OR-reduction from per-entry bits is entirely absent. Software that configures per-entry error suppression expects those transactions to be silently dropped, but they will still generate bus errors.

RegMapIO exports only o_reg_hwcfg0_enable and o_reg_hwcfg0_no_w but not o_reg_hwcfg0_peis or o_reg_hwcfg0_pees. The PEIS/PEES capability bits are readable via the CSR map (reg_hwcfg0.toUInt includes them at line 516), but they are not wired to the Ctrl module where per-entry interrupt and error suppression decisions are made. This architectural gap means even if a developer wanted to add proper PEIS/PEES gating, the signal doesn't reach the consumer. This is a design-level deficiency that codifies the other violations.
findings.snippet:
val o_reg_hwcfg0_enable = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_hwcfg0_no_w = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_hwcfg1_rrid_num = Output(UInt(16.W))
val o_reg_hwcfg2_prio_entry = Output(UInt(16.W))
val o_reg_errcfg_ie = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_errcfg_rs = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_errcfg_msi_en = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_errcfg_msidata = Output(UInt(11.W))
val o_reg_errinfo_v = Output(UInt(1.W))
val o_reg_errinfo_ttype = Output(UInt(2.W))

findings.finding: IopmpParams.peis=1 and IopmpParams.pees=0 are correctly mapped into RegHwcfg0 initialization at lines 485-486. The bit positions in toUInt (line 516: Cat(..., pees, peis, ...)) place PEES and PEIS adjacent in the hwcfg0 register word. For the current hardcoded parameter set, the reset values are correct and self-consistent with the hardware implementation (PEIS supported, PEES not supported). The HWCFG0.pees=0 accurately reflects that per-entry error suppression is unimplemented in the Ctrl FSM — this CSR bit is truthful.
findings.snippet:
val peis               = 1    // [R   ] PEIS enabled
val pees               = 0    // [R   ] PEES enabled

findings.finding: EntryAttribute bundle correctly defines all suppression fields (sire, siwe, sixe, sere, sewe, sexe) as 1-bit UInts matching the IOPMP spec entry_cfg bit layout. The EntryTable correctly reads these from tmp_entry_cfg at bit positions 5 (sire), 6 (siwe), 7 (sixe), 8 (sere), 9 (sewe), 10 (sexe) at lines 431-436. The field definitions themselves are well-formed — the bugs are entirely in the Ctrl consumer.
